items.samenvatting_bron: Urbanisation in Lagos Metropolis has increased the rate of creating high-density urban centres, thus aggravating energy demands and environmental pressures. It is in this paper that we have evaluated how urban design tools can help to reduce energy use in high-density developments in Lagos. With the Compact City Theory, Sustainable Urban Development Theory, Urban Metabolism Theory and Climate-Responsive Urban Design Theory, we used a descriptive and analytic design and preferred quantitative approaches in a mixed-method approach. The data were collected in the form of structured questionnaires filled by 384 participants, with the supplement of the information by the direct observation and GIS-based spatial analysis of the three purposely chosen high-density districts, Victoria Island, Ikeja GRA, and Surulere. items.titel: Electrocution events of Mico rondoni (Primates: Cebidae) in the city of Porto Velho, Rondônia, Brazil
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Urbanization and habitat fragmentation expose arboreal wildlife to electrical infrastructure in Porto Velho, Rondônia state, Brazil. This study describes four fatal electrocution events involving Mico rondoni and examines the circumstances associated with the accidents. During seven months of monitoring in the Floresta neighborhood, all four deaths involved adults from the same group and occurred at a single recurrent site. The animals showed burns on the hands and feet, and one sustained trauma after falling. The concentration of events at one power-line location identifies a local electrocution hotspot but does not establish the frequency or population-level importance of this threat across the species’ range. The cases support site-specific mitigation, including technical assessment and insulation of hazardous electrical components, combined with monitored canopy crossings. Broader surveillance is required before the relevance of electrocution to M. rondoni conservation can be determined.

items.titel: The short-beaked echidna in South-East Queensland: regional data gaps and conservation risks
items.samenvatting_bron: The short-beaked echidna (Tachyglossus aculeatus) is widely distributed across Australia and is often described as common, yet robust information on abundance, demography and population trends remains sparse across much of its mainland range. This evidence gap is particularly important in South-East Queensland (SEQ), where rapid urban expansion, habitat fragmentation, dense road networks, climatic warming and the spread of the red imported fire ant (Solenopsis invicta, RIFA) may interact with the species’ slow-breeding life history. Together, these pressures could affect regional population status, while current datasets provide limited capacity to detect change. This review synthesises current knowledge relevant to echidna vulnerability and detectability and evaluates the evidence base available for SEQ, drawing on citizen science observations, wildlife hospital records and the limited peer-reviewed field studies from the region.
